title: Automated Firebreak: smoke + progressive-load guardian for private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an automated "firebreak" runner that executes a deterministic sequence of post-deploy health checks for Private (VPC) deployments. The runner will validate API readiness, exercise model load paths, and perform progressive smoke-to-load ramps that can automatically flag or block rollout if SLOs are violated. This ticket covers Terraform wiring for orchestration IAM and schedules, the test harness for API + model handshakes, and a minimal rollback signal integration with the rollout controller.
acceptance_criteria: Runner can be triggered by Terraform null_resource after deployment and returns structured pass/fail status to rollout controller
API handshake test completes within 5s for control-plane API and 30s for model node initialization across 95% of runs
Model priming sequence loads a sample model shard, warms KV cache, and verifies token inference for a smoke prompt without exceeding memory target
Progressive load ramp achieves predefined QPS steps (1 -> 10 -> 50) and aborts rollout if latency P95 or error-rate thresholds breached
All artifacts (logs, traces, and synthetic metrics) are archived to the per-deployment object store with links surfaced in the console
runbook: 1) Terraform applies the module that creates a scheduled Lambda-like executor (or cron job on the deploy container). 2) Executor pulls the latest post-deploy harness image and runs the canonical smoke script. 3) Smoke script performs: API handshake, model load, warmup prompts, small synthetic QPS ramp, and a final health summary POST to rollout endpoint. 4) Rollout controller consumes the summary and decides pass/fail. 5) On failure, controller triggers firebreak: halt traffic, notify on-call, and revert to previous stable model/route.
implementation_notes: Expose a minimal immutable status payload: {status, failed_checks[], metrics_url}
Use existing terraform module 'deploy.exec-scheduler' and add iam bindings limited to 'putObject' on deploy artifact bucket
Model warmup should use short deterministic prompts from the 'warmup-set' S3 file to avoid nondeterministic outputs
Integrate trace IDs into logs so Console can pin traces to specific harness runs
test_plan: Local: run harness against dev VPC image and validate exit codes and artifact upload. Staging: integrate into staging deployment pipeline and run three consecutive executions; record metrics to synthetic-run dashboard. Canary: enable runner in a single customer tenant during a non-peak window; monitor P95 and error rate for 30 minutes post-checks.
test_results: 2026-03-05: local run passed (3/3 checks), artifacts uploaded. 2026-03-09: staging run 1 failed during model load on rtx-a100-40 due to ephemeral disk pressure (investigation linked). 2026-03-11: staging rerun after tmpfs tweak passed full sequence.
rollout_policy: On first failure: mark canary as unhealthy and stop rollout. If failures are transient and subsequent runs pass (n=2), rollout may resume manually. For deterministic failures tied to terraform-provisioned resources, rollback to previous infra snapshot must be initiated.
